notes: Produced a PID controller tuned for the 7-sensor symmetric layout with larger sensor coverage, maintaining previous gains and line loss strategy. This aims to reduce line loss events and improve lateral line detection, especially on challenging tracks like the slalom.
rationale: The previous iteration increased sensor size to 0.016 m, widened the wheel track to 0.16 m, and reduced mass to 0.7 kg, aiming to reduce line loss events and steering oscillation while improving acceleration and progress. However, race data shows persistent line loss events (0.35-0.4) and no finishes on the slalom track, indicating coverage and stability issues remain. Steering oscillation is still moderate to high (0.37-0.45), and control effort has increased, suggesting the controller is working harder to maintain line tracking. To address this, I propose adding two additional sensors to the array (increasing from 5 to 7) to improve lateral line coverage and reduce line loss events, especially in complex track sections. Sensor size remains at 0.016 m to maintain good coverage and noise tolerance. Wheel track remains at 0.16 m to preserve stability benefits. Mass remains at 0.7 kg to retain acceleration advantages. Sensor positions are symmetrically spaced across the front, extending coverage laterally to better detect line edges and reduce loss. Wheel radius, body width, and body length remain unchanged to isolate sensor geometry effects. The controller is tuned with PID gains (kp=8.0, ki=0.5, kd=2.0) balancing responsiveness and stability. Sensor weights emphasize outer sensors with opposite signs to center sensors to generate a strong steering signal. Base speed is set to 1.5 to encourage good progress without risking instability. The line loss strategy is 'last_direction' to maintain steering when the line is lost, aiding recovery. The observation request includes all key metrics to evaluate tracking quality and control effort as requested by the builder.
